question.latex: An electromagnetic wave travelling in x-direction is described by field equation $E_y = 300 \sin \omega \left$t - \frac{x}{c}\right$$. If the electron is restricted to move in y-direction only with speed of $1.5 \times 10^6\text{ m/s}$ then ratio of maximum electric and magnetic forces acting on the electron is _______.
question.unicode: An electromagnetic wave travelling in x-direction is described by field equation E_y = 300 sin omega leftt - (x/c)right. If the electron is restricted to move in y-direction only with speed of 1.5 × 10^6text{ m/s} then ratio of maximum electric and magnetic forces acting on the electron is _______.
question.plainText: An electromagnetic wave travelling in x-direction is described by field equation E_y = 300 sin omega leftt - (x)/(c)right. If the electron is restricted to move in y-direction only with speed of 1.5 times 10^6text{ m/s} then ratio of maximum electric and magnetic forces acting on the electron is _______.

explanation.latex:
In an electromagnetic wave in vacuum, the amplitudes of the electric field ($E_0$) and magnetic field ($B_0$) are related by $E_0 = c B_0$, where $c$ is the speed of light.
The maximum electric force on the electron is $F_E = e E_0$.
The maximum magnetic force on the electron moving with speed $v$ is $F_B = e v B_0 \sin(90^\circ) = e v B_0$ (since the electron moves in the y-direction and magnetic field is in the z-direction, they are mutually perpendicular).
The ratio of the maximum electric force to the maximum magnetic force is:
$\frac{F_E}{F_B} = \frac{e E_0}{e v B_0} = \frac{E_0}{v B_0}$
Substitute $E_0 = c B_0$:
$\frac{F_E}{F_B} = \frac{c B_0}{v B_0} = \frac{c}{v}$
Given $c = 3 \times 10^8\text{ m/s}$ and $v = 1.5 \times 10^6\text{ m/s}$:
$\frac{F_E}{F_B} = \frac{3 \times 10^8}{1.5 \times 10^6} = 2 \times 10^2 = 200$.
